Key observations from the test image:
- Soybean stems split lengthwise, showing internal pith
- **Pith is white/cream colored** — not brown
- Stem exterior shows numerous tiny black specks/dots
- Stems appear dried/mature

The **white pith** is a critical diagnostic feature pointing to Sudden Death Syndrome. Let me compare with reference images for top candidates.

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Soybean stems split lengthwise, showing **white/cream-colored pith** inside; stem exterior has numerous tiny black specks/dots; appears to be a diagnostic split-stem demonstration
- **Key features**: white pith, black specks on exterior, split-stem presentation

**Candidate comparison:**

| Feature | SDS | Charcoal Rot | Diaporthe |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pith color when split | **White** (diagnostic) | Charcoal/dark (microsclerotia in pith) | White visible in reference |
| Exterior specks | Bluish fungal growth possible | Black microsclerotia on surface | Black pycnidia (linear rows) |
| Stem demonstration | Split-stem test = white pith | Split-stem shows charcoal pith | Linear black specks on surface |

The **white pith** in the split stem is explicitly described as the key diagnostic for **Sudden Death Syndrome** — "Stems of SDS-infected plants have white pith (distinguishing from brown stem rot which causes brown discoloration of the pith)." The Charcoal Rot reference images (top-left) did show a similar split-stem presentation, but Charcoal Rot produces *charcoal-colored* pith with dark microsclerotia throughout, not white. The SDS description specifically calls out white pith as the canonical distinguishing feature.
